scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Minimal models in numerical dimension one” (preprints/Minimal-models-in-numerical-dimension-one-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 036 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6fe4b337ba8c9128), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X be a smooth connected complex projective variety of dimension n ≥ 3. Suppose that KX is pseudo-effective and κσ(X, KX) = 1, with the convention (1.1). Then there are a normal projective Q-factorial terminal variety Y with KY nef and a finite sequence ϕ : X 99K Y of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips. The inverse of ϕ contracts no prime divisor. On a common smooth projective resolution p : W → X, q : W → Y , compatible canonical divisors satisfy (1.2) p∗ KX = q∗ KY + E, where E is an effective q-exceptional Q-divisor whose support contains the strict transform of every prime divisor of X contracted by ϕ.
